title: Delegate a contract-bounded implementation
summary: Freeze an implementation brief, terminology snapshot, Markdown contract units, and Git basis; plan and delegate finite implementation packets through Nucleus; independently review them; and return one exact reviewed candidate.
use_when: The caller has an authorized implementation brief, an applicable frozen terminology snapshot, one or more complete caller-enumerated Markdown contract units, an exact Git repository, and suitable validation gates.
Implementation work should be decomposed before mutation, assigned to bounded agents, and accepted only by independent review against the frozen contract basis.
Interrupted orchestration must remain durable and recoverable without silently changing inputs or inventing another audit cycle.
do_not_use_when: Requirements, system authority, contract-unit boundaries, terminology grounding, repository permission, or the intended validation gates remain materially unsettled.
The request is only to inspect, resume, cancel, retry, initialize, diagnose, install, release, deploy, push, or apply an existing candidate.
A general workflow engine, deployment coordinator, release gate, unbounded audit, direct Codex invocation, or non-Git mutation target is required.
outcome: One durable succeeded Vizier run bound to an exact integrated Git candidate whose accepted delegation, independently accepted packet candidates, configured gates, and independent integrated review all apply to the same frozen input basis, or an explicit needs-attention or cancelled outcome.
effects: Copies exact caller-selected Markdown into the private ledger, resolves the selected Git source, creates and mutates Vizier-owned isolated worktrees, freezes Git candidates, and records workflow transitions and evidence.

Submits bounded planner, assembler, plan-reviewer, implementor, packet-reviewer, integrator, and integrated-reviewer jobs to Nucleus, each explicitly requesting requester-owned `gpt-5.6-sol` with reasoning effort `max`, and may consume Codex account allowance.

Gives packet implementors packet-local checks only, then runs caller-supplied configured gates after packet review and integration through the host CI broker against the exact integrated candidate and binds every result to that candidate.
Does not move the caller's branch, apply the candidate there, push, release, deploy, amend requirements, or mutate Pratica or Semantics.
authority: The caller owns the implementation request, contract and terminology meaning, selected source and gate authority, and every later delivery action.
Vizier owns run admission, exact document identity, the work graph, workspace isolation, candidate and review binding, retry policy, gates, and run success.
Nucleus owns execution and transport only; agents author proposed Markdown and source changes but cannot advance Vizier state except through a validated expected result.
success: Every planner result, assembled delegation, implementation handoff, candidate, review disposition, and gate result required by the run is durably committed and bound to its exact inputs.

No implementor or integrator accepts its own edits, every required packet candidate is accepted, every configured gate succeeds on the exact integrated candidate, and one independent integrated reviewer accepts that candidate.
The terminal run reports `succeeded` and the exact result candidate; Nucleus completion or final prose alone never satisfies this condition.
failure_and_recovery: After interruption, inspect the exact run and use wait or resume; Vizier reuses only persisted requests and committed managed-tool results.
A blocking finding must cite an existing contract or accepted packet criterion. Unstated requirements, missing authority or evidence, and wider scope leave needs-attention rather than becoming code.

Changes requested create only a bounded successor of the same review-subject type and a targeted recheck bound to that successor and persisted submitted scope; it cannot silently widen into unrelated packets or contract units. Exhaustion, an unsafe worktree, unresolvable integration conflict, failed gate, lost attempt, or invalid result remains explicit and never triggers an unbounded retry or direct-Codex fallback.
privacy: The ledger, worktrees, Git objects, and correlated Nucleus state may contain complete private implementation and repository material.
Vizier minimizes each role's workspace and documents, disables web and launch-context disclosure, and does not place private run bodies in Chancery, release bundles, or routine logs.

interfaces.label: Submit implementation run
interfaces.invocation: /Users/joey/.local/bin/vizier [--database ABS] [--json] run submit --repository ABS --brief FILE --terminology FILE --contract ID=FILE... [--gate NAME=COMMAND...] [--source REV] [--request-key KEY] [--remediation-rounds N]

does_not_authorize: Changing requirements, accepting an unanchored review preference, operating Pratica or Semantics, or exposing material beyond the exact role boundary.
Applying the candidate to the caller's branch, pushing, publishing, releasing, deploying, or changing another product or service.
Automatically retrying terminal work, restarting Nucleus, reading Nucleus SQLite or credentials, or invoking Codex outside Nucleus.

consumers.statement: An authorized local caller with a complete frozen implementation basis may request one finite, durable, independently reviewed Git implementation candidate.
Requirements discovery, general workflow automation, deployment, release, push, candidate application, and non-Git mutation are outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: The selected private ledger is initialized and healthy; the repository and Git source are valid and caller-authorized; brief, terminology, and ordered contract files are readable exact UTF-8 Markdown; at least one contract is supplied; gates and remediation policy are finite; and strict compatible Nucleus readiness is green.
The caller obtained the applicable Semantics snapshot through its supported read interface, wrapped it unchanged as the terminology Markdown, and considers it current for this run.

inputs.statement: Inputs are one absolute Git repository, optional exact Git revision, exact brief and terminology files, ordered unique ID-to-contract-file pairs, zero or more unique named gate commands, optional request key, and a bounded positive remediation-round count.
Implicit requirement extraction, mutable latest-document selectors, arbitrary Nucleus fields, credentials, direct Semantics state, and non-Git targets are unsupported inputs.

outputs.statement: Output identifies the durable run, its exact frozen basis and current state, attempts and documents, review and gate evidence, and on success the exact integrated Git candidate.
Output is not an applied branch, push, release, deployment, Pratica amendment, Semantics update, or guarantee that an external consumer accepts the change.

data_semantics.statement: Meaning-bearing documents are exact opaque Markdown; structured state covers only identity, digest, order, lineage, packet links and dependencies, roles, jobs, workspaces, candidates, dispositions, gate results, and lifecycle.

Accepted permits one exact review subject to advance, changes_requested permits bounded remediation of anchored findings through a successor of the same subject type, blocked requires caller resolution, and advisories create no work.

identity_and_units.statement: Run, document, packet, invocation, attempt, review, and candidate IDs identify distinct records; SHA-256 binds exact document or request bytes; Git object identity binds source; remediation rounds and gate results are counted per run.
Nucleus requester.program is `vizier`, requester.id is the stable run ID, and each persisted job ID is the idempotency identity for one exact request.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A succeeded run covers the complete frozen ordered contract set through its accepted delegation, required packet candidates, gates, and integrated review, all bound to the same exact source and document identities.
Vizier does not discover missing contracts, refresh terminology, prove repository state remains unchanged after result publication, or claim that no other useful concern exists.

access.statement: The current-user CLI accesses the selected private ledger and authorized Git repository; planners and reviewers use exact read-only checkouts, writers use disjoint read-write worktrees, and Nucleus jobs use explicit role-specific permissions with web and launch context disabled.
Direct SQLite access, direct Codex fallback, hidden repository discovery, credential access, remote service control, and shared writable worktrees are unsupported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Run admission atomically binds exact inputs before execution; managed-tool results commit idempotently before acknowledgement; every review names an exact immutable review subject, with plan review bound to the assembled delegation overview, packet graph, and current packet-plan revision rather than provisional unit plans, and packet or integrated review bound to a Git candidate; and restart recovery resumes persisted work rather than reconstructing it from model prose.
Automatic remediation is finite, cancellation records intent without undoing committed state, and terminal needs-attention preserves evidence for explicit caller recovery.

operational_limits.statement: One run has one broad review of the assembled delegation, packet graph, and current packet plans, one broad review for each packet candidate, one broad integrated review, and at most the submitted remediation rounds of persisted-scope targeted recheck; ready jobs share Nucleus's eight global slots without reservation.
No planning quality, model quality, start time, completion time, throughput, repository size, retained-state size, gate duration, or availability objective is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 binds the version-one ledger and managed-tool meanings, Nucleus protocol and execution contract range, opaque Markdown rule, independent-review invariant, finite remediation, and exact Git candidate result.
No perpetual support window, migration horizon, model stability, Git compatibility window, or deprecation period is promised.

reliances.statement: Vizier relies on Nucleus for strict admission, authenticated bounded Codex execution, cancellation, durable job evidence, and managed-tool transport while retaining all workflow and domain-success authority.
The caller relies on Semantics to read the applicable terminology repository and supplies the resulting snapshot to Vizier as frozen opaque Markdown; Vizier has no live Semantics runtime call.
Candidate creation and integration rely on Git command and object behavior, but no dedicated installed Chancery contract describes that boundary.
